searchDocs.title: Adding Competition Volunteer to the system​
searchDocs.content: Choose the Staff member tab, fill in the form and click Add person. You can also assign a card to them (read more about assigning cards here).    To let a volunteer sign in to the panel, create an account for them, see Accounts.

searchDocs.title: Adding a competitor competing only in unofficial events to the system​
searchDocs.content: If you want to add a competitor who is competing only in unofficial events, choose the Competitor tab and fill in the form. You can get their data from the WCA by entering their WCA ID and clicking Get person data from WCA. You can scan their card here as well.    warning Use this form only for competitors competing only in unofficial events. If you want to add a competitor who registered on the spot, do it on the WCA website and click Sync with WCA in Setup → Competition.

searchDocs.title: Roles​
searchDocs.content: Role	What they can doStaff	View the panel, check in competitors and assign cards Stage leader	Staff, plus attendance and marking competitors as not coming, in the rooms they're given (see Stage leaders and rooms) Organizer	Stage leader, plus devices, setup (competition settings, users, unofficial events), adding persons and running groups Delegate	Organizer, plus incidents, scrambles, all results tools, tutorial mode and running a different round on a station Admin	Everything, including server logs, device logs and uploading firmware  You can't give anyone a role higher than your own: an organizer can't create delegates or admins.  A delegate can also give a user who isn't a delegate or admin delegate access for one group. While it lasts, that user gets Incidents and can resolve the incidents of that group, with only the actions the delegate allowed. Their role doesn't change, and the access ends by itself when the group ends.

searchDocs.title: Creating an account​
searchDocs.content: Users can be added after the competition is imported. Go to Setup → Users and click Create user. Choose between the FKMTime Account and WCA Login tabs.

searchDocs.title: FKMTime Account​
searchDocs.content: Fill in Username, Full name, Password and Roles and click Create. For a stage leader, also choose their rooms (see below). User will be able to sign in with the username and password you provided.

searchDocs.title: WCA Login​
searchDocs.content: Search for a person, select roles (and rooms, for a stage leader) and click Create. User will be able to sign in with their WCA account and will have the roles you selected.

searchDocs.title: Stage leaders and rooms​
searchDocs.content: A stage leader takes attendance in the rooms you give them, so a stage leader of one room can't change another room's attendance by picking the wrong group.  When you give someone the Stage leader role, choose under Takes attendance in either All rooms or the rooms they cover. You can't create the account until something is ticked. If the competition has only one room, the field doesn't show and they cover all rooms. Organizers, delegates and admins always cover all rooms, so the field doesn't show for them either.  The users list shows the rooms after the role, e.g. Stage leader · Side Hall. To move a stage leader to another room, for example on the next day, edit the user and change their rooms.  A stage leader with some rooms:  sees only those rooms' groups on the Attendance page, and "Attendance" only on their rooms on the home page, the schedule and a person's page,can mark someone as not coming for the rest of the day if one of that person's groups that day is in their rooms; it applies to the whole day, other rooms included,still sees the attendance statistics and the most missed assignments for the whole competition.  A room's groups are the ones the schedule puts in it, plus any group the room has run, so a group moved to another room on the day belongs to both.  Stage leaders added before this existed cover all rooms until you change them.

searchDocs.title: Managing accounts​
searchDocs.content: Each user in the list has actions to Edit user (roles, a stage leader's rooms, and username and full name of FKMTime accounts), Change password (FKMTime accounts only) and Delete user.  When a password changes, every session signed in with the old password ends. Users who are deleted or whose roles change are disconnected within a few seconds and see the panel with their new access.  Users with an FKMTime account can change their own password on the Settings page.

searchDocs.title: Access to competition​
searchDocs.content: If someone who signs in with a WCA account doesn't manage the competition and wasn't added on the Users page, they can't sign in ("You are not allowed to manage this competition"). Add them as delegate/organizer on the WCA website (FKMTime checks it with the WCA on every sign-in), or add their WCA account as described above.

searchDocs.title: How updates work?
searchDocs.content: How updates work? We use GitHub Releases to distribute updates. You have to turn on Update devices in Setup → Competition (the Devices card). After that, turn on all devices and micro-connector. Micro-connector checks for new updates every 5 minutes and if there is a new update, it will automatically download it and send it to all devices. warning Turn Update devices off while the competition is in progress, and do not turn off device while updating! Admins can also upload a firmware file by hand on the Devices page, in the Upload firmware tab. Devices update to it when Update devices is on.

searchDocs.title: Enter your Wi-Fi data​
searchDocs.content: Go to Setup → Competition (or click Device settings on the Devices page) and fill in the Network card:  WiFi SSID and WiFi password - the network the devices should joinAuto server discovery - devices find the server with mDNS. Turn it off only if mDNS doesn't work in your network, and enter the micro-connector ws URL instead  Click Save at the bottom of the page.

searchDocs.title: If your machine supports bluetooth​
searchDocs.content: Go to the Devices page and click Auto setup. For the next 5 minutes, micro-connector writes the Wi-Fi data to new devices over Bluetooth. After that, devices will be able to communicate with backend by Wi-Fi through micro-connector.

searchDocs.title: If your machine doesn't support bluetooth​
searchDocs.content: Turn on the device and connect to the hotspot it creates. Its name is FKM-XXXX (the same name is shown on the device) and it has no password. A setup page opens on its own; if it doesn't, go to 192.168.4.1. Enter the Network name (SSID) and Password, set Auto server discovery (mDNS) (or enter the WebSocket URL) the same way as in the panel, and click Connect to Network.

searchDocs.title: After entering Wi-Fi data​
searchDocs.content: To connect a new device, press the submit button on it. The Devices page then shows New device wants to connect with its ESP ID. Click Add, fill in the Create device form (name, and room, type and hardware version when there is more than one to choose from) and click Add. A device that was added before shows wants to reconnect instead; click Reconnect.    You can also add a device by hand with Add device, if you know its ESP ID.

searchDocs.title: Managing devices​
searchDocs.content: Each device shows its battery, Wi-Fi signal, firmware version and how many solves it recorded. Click the number of solves to see every solve the device recorded. If a station hits an error, an icon next to it shows the error and how to fix it.    Device actions:  Edit device - change name, room or typeStart tutorial (delegates, stations only) - the station takes practice solves that are never saved, so newcomers can try it. It ends by itself 15 minutes after the station was last used, or with End tutorialRun a different round… (delegates, stations only) - the station takes attempts for another round than its room's groups, until you click Back to the room's roundView logs (admins) - live logs of the deviceDelete device - a device that already recorded solves is retired instead, so its solves keep their station. Retired devices are listed under Retired devices and can be restored

searchDocs.title: Buy proper cards​
searchDocs.content: You will need to buy RFID cards with 13.56 MHz frequency.

searchDocs.title: Assign cards to the competitors​
searchDocs.content: Go to the Persons page and open the Assign cards tab. It lists only people without a card, and the search is ready to type in.  Search for the competitor, pick them, scan the card you want to assign to them (it fills the Card ID field) and press Enter or click Assign. Search for the next competitor and repeat the process.    To assign or change the card of one person, use Assign card in their row on the All persons tab.

searchDocs.title: Check-in​
searchDocs.content: FKMTime has a check-in system that allows you to keep track of who is present at the competition and got their ID (or any other things).  To start, go to the Check in page. It shows how many competitors are already checked in.

searchDocs.title: Cards assigned before the competition​
searchDocs.content: If you assigned cards to the competitors before the competition, just scan the competitor's card. Their details open; press Enter or scan the same card again to check them in.

searchDocs.title: Cards not assigned before the competition​
searchDocs.content: If you didn't assign cards to the competitors before the competition, search for the competitor by name or WCA ID, scan a card to assign it to them, and click Check in and assign card.

searchDocs.title: Newcomers​
searchDocs.content: If you are checking in a newcomer, you have to check that their data matches their document (passport, driver's license, etc.). FKMTime shows the Newcomer checks list: name, date of birth, that they are a newcomer, and citizenship. You have to tick every check before you can check them in.    After each check-in you can undo it, and the most recent check-ins are listed under Just checked in.

searchDocs.title: How to add an unofficial event?​
searchDocs.content: Go to Setup → Unofficial events.    Click Add unofficial event, select the event and set up its rounds: format, time limit (and whether it is cumulative) and cutoff. You can add up to 4 rounds.    Click Add unofficial event. That's it! Now everything works the same as for official events.  You can change the rounds later with Edit rounds, or remove the event with Delete event.

searchDocs.title: Entering unofficial events results into Cubing Contests​
searchDocs.content: If you want to enter unofficial events results into Cubing Contests, you need to enter the CubingContests token in the competition settings, see Importing competition.

searchDocs.title: Changing groups automatically​
searchDocs.content: You can opt for doing it automatically, by turning on Change groups automatically in Setup → Competition (the Competition day card). If so, the group will be automatically changed to the next one from the schedule once all its results are entered and there are no unresolved incidents. Competitors marked as Not coming don't hold the group up.

searchDocs.title: Changing groups manually​
searchDocs.content: Although it is recommended to turn on Change groups automatically, you are not forced to do so. Organizers and delegates can start groups from the room's card on the Home page.  The card shows the running group, how many results are entered, what the group is still waiting for, and the room's next group from the schedule under Next. Once the running group is done, click the start button (for example Start group 2, or Start 3x3 R2 · Group 1 when the next group is in another round) and confirm. Stations in the room switch to the new group right away.    When two or more rooms are ready, Next group in all rooms starts the next group in each of them at once.  The room's More (…) menu has:  Change group… - pick any event, round and group. You can also run several groups in one room at the same time (Run both), for example when holding multiple events at the same timeBack to the previous groupGive delegate access… (delegates only) - let someone resolve the incidents of the room's running or next group, see Delegate access for one groupStop a single group, when the room runs several of themStop the room

searchDocs.title: Opening rounds​
searchDocs.content: Results can only be entered once their round is open on the results website:  WCA Live - after a group starts a new round, FKMTime reminds you to open the round in WCA Live.WCA Integrated Live Results - FKMTime opens first rounds itself. Later rounds are opened automatically if Open later rounds automatically is on in the competition settings. Otherwise FKMTime asks you to open them, and the Home page warns about rounds that aren't open yet.

searchDocs.title: Home page alerts​
searchDocs.content: Above the room cards, the Home page shows alerts when something needs doing. Organizers and delegates see them, except No delegate free, which only delegates see. The buttons that start or end tutorial mode are for delegates.    Tutorial for new competitors (or the name of the schedule's tutorial activity) - from 15 minutes before a tutorial in the schedule until it ends, suggests putting a station in tutorial mode, so newcomers can try a solve without anything being saved. Start tutorial (or Start tutorial on a station) starts it; the × (Dismiss) hides the suggestion.… is in tutorial mode / N stations are in tutorial mode - stations whose solves aren't saved. End tutorial takes a station out of tutorial mode.No delegate free for … / No delegate free for N groups - every delegate competes in a running or next group. Give delegate access… lets someone else resolve that group's incidents, see Delegate access for one group.N competitors didn't come to … - with WCA Integrated Live Results, a finished round lists competitors who never came. Until they're removed there, the next round can't open. Untick anyone allowed to compete late and click Remove from … in WCA Integrated Live Results.Not connected to WCA Integrated Live Results (or WCA Integrated Live Results disconnected) - results can't reach the WCA website. Connect in settings (or Reconnect in settings) opens the settings.Some results aren't reaching WCA live results - per round, results still sending after a few minutes or not taken. Each round links to its results, where every result says why.  Each room card shows, besides the running group and its progress:  Incidents (delegates only) - the room's open incidents, each with ResolveRecent results - the latest attempts of the round running in the roomstations of the room that run another round (… is running …), with Back to the room's round (delegates only)what the group is waiting for: competitors still solving, incidents to resolve, extras to do, and who hasn't started yet, with Not coming for those who take attendance in the room. When the room moves on by itself, it also says when

searchDocs.title: Competition settings​
searchDocs.content: The settings are split into cards. After changing anything, click Save in the bar at the bottom of the page.

searchDocs.title: Results​
searchDocs.content: FKMTime sends official results where the competition's scoretaking setting on the WCA website says. Official results go to shows what it is: WCA Live, WCA Integrated Live Results or Nowhere. To change it, use Change on the WCA website, then click Check again.    WCA Live​  You will need a scoretaking token that can be taken from WCA Live. Go to the account page and generate one. This token may expire after 7 days and is specific to the selected competition. Paste it into the Scoretaking token field.  FKMTime reminds you at the top of the page if the token is missing or may have expired.  WCA Integrated Live Results​  Click Connect to WCA Integrated Live Results and sign in with a WCA account that can enter scores for the competition. Results will be entered as this account. You can add more scoretakers by WCA ID in the Scoretakers card.  Turn on Open later rounds automatically if FKMTime should open later rounds itself. Otherwise FKMTime suggests opening them and a person confirms, because opening a round locks the round before it.  When to send results​  By default, results are sent after every solve (Send after every solve). If the internet connection in the venue is not stable you can choose Send active rounds results every 5 minutes, or turn sending off completely with Do not send (for testing purposes).  Cubing Contests​  If you plan to host unofficial events and want to send results automatically to Cubing Contests, copy the token from Cubing Contests and paste it into the CubingContests token field.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: rfid_task calls pcd_init() and checks pcd_is_init() in a loop. When the reader does not respond, this error is logged once and the task keeps retrying every RFID_RETRY_INIT_MS milliseconds. The rest of the firmware (Wi-Fi, WebSocket, display) continues running normally — only RFID scanning is blocked until the reader initialises successfully.  The same retry loop runs again each time the device wakes from sleep.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The RFID chip is not responding over its bus (I²C on v4, SPI on v3). This can happen transiently on the very first boot after power-on while the chip is still settling.The RFID module is defective or was damaged.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Power-cycle the device — This is the standard fix mentioned in the firmware log itself. Remove power completely, wait a few seconds, and power back on.Check for repeated failures — If E1 appears in the error log on every boot and the device never recovers RFID scanning, the RFID chip may be faulty. Contact support or replace the device.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: battery_read_task exits immediately. The device loses battery state-of-charge monitoring — the battery percentage will not be shown on the display or reported to the server. All other functionality continues normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The BQ27441 fuel gauge is not responding on the I²C bus. This can happen if the battery was disconnected before boot.The fuel gauge IC is defective.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Ensure the battery is connected — If the battery was removed or disconnected, reconnect it and reboot. The firmware even logs "Battery was removed before boot!" if state-of-charge reads as 0 after init.Reboot the device — A fresh boot retries the task.Contact support — If this error appears consistently with the battery properly connected, the fuel gauge IC may be faulty. Open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and that battery read is skipped. Battery state-of-charge monitoring continues on the next cycle, but the percentage shown on the display and reported to the server may be stale until a read succeeds. All other functionality continues normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The fuel gauge is not responding on the I²C bus — for example, if the battery was disconnected or the connection is intermittent.Another peripheral on the shared I²C bus is holding the bus or not releasing it, blocking the battery gauge transaction.A transient electrical fault or noise on the I²C lines.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Ensure the battery is connected — Reseat or reconnect the battery and reboot.Reboot the device — Clears a stuck bus state and retries all peripherals.Contact support — If this error appears frequently with the battery properly connected, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: rfid_task exits immediately. RFID scanning is unavailable for this session — the device will not scan any competitor cards until it is rebooted. All other functionality (Wi-Fi, display, Stackmat) continues normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The SPI peripheral configuration failed at driver level, which should not happen on unmodified firmware.Flash or firmware corruption produced invalid peripheral parameters.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — A fresh boot re-runs rfid_task from scratch.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware using espflash to rule out a corrupted build.Contact support — If this error appears consistently on stock firmware, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and the firmware continues anyway. lcd_task does not exit — it attempts to keep running. However, display output may be corrupted or absent since the driver did not start cleanly.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The display cable is disconnected or not properly seated. The display is connected via cable on v4 hardware.The OLED module is defective.A transient I²C/SPI communication error during the brief init sequence.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Check the display cable — Power off the device and reseat the cable between the display and the PCB.Reboot the device — A transient init error may not repeat on a fresh boot.Contact support — If the display is consistently blank or garbled after reboot, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: stackmat_task exits immediately. The device will not receive time readings from the wired Stackmat timer for this session. All other firmware tasks continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The UART peripheral could not be configured at 1200 baud for the Stackmat RX pin. This should not happen on unmodified firmware — it may indicate a corrupted firmware build.The Stackmat cable is causing a short on the UART RX pin during startup.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Disconnect the Stackmat cable and reboot — If the error disappears, the cable or Stackmat timer may be causing a signal issue on the UART RX line.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware using espflash to rule out a corrupted build.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this recurs consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: lcd_task exits immediately. The display will show nothing for this session. All other firmware tasks (RFID, Wi-Fi, WebSocket) continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Not enough contiguous heap memory was available to allocate the framebuffer. This can happen if heap fragmentation from a previous crash left the heap in a degraded state.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — A clean boot resets the heap. This almost always resolves a one-off allocation failure.Update the firmware — Newer firmware versions may reduce peak heap usage.Contact support — If this error appears on every cold boot with the latest firmware, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and that frame update is dropped. lcd_task keeps running, but the display may show a stale or partially updated image until the next successful flush. All other firmware tasks continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The display cable is loose or not properly seated.Another peripheral on the shared I²C bus is blocking or delaying transactions.The OLED module is defective or not responding.A transient I²C communication fault.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Check the display cable — Power off the device and reseat the cable between the display and the PCB.Reboot the device — Clears a stuck bus state and retries the display driver.Contact support — If the display is consistently frozen, garbled, or fails to update after reboot, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: rfid_task exits immediately. RFID scanning is unavailable for this session. All other firmware tasks continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Setting the chip-select (CS) pin high failed during bus setup, which indicates a GPIO or shift-register issue.Flash or firmware corruption produced invalid pin assignments.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — A fresh boot retries the whole rfid_task setup.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware using espflash.Contact support — If this error appears consistently, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: rfid_task exits immediately. RFID scanning is unavailable for this session. All other firmware tasks continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Heap memory exhaustion at startup prevented the DMA buffer allocation.A firmware bug or corrupted build produced an invalid DMA configuration.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — Frees memory and retries.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware using espflash with a full chip erase.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this recurs consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: main enters an infinite loop — it logs the error and waits 1 second, forever. The device is effectively halted; it will not proceed to Wi-Fi or any other functionality until it is reflashed. This is the only error that causes a true firmware halt.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The device was flashed with only an application binary, without also writing the correct partition table. The partition table in flash is from an older or incompatible firmware version.A manual flash operation using esptool or a similar tool wrote the wrong binary to the wrong address.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reflash with the full image — Use espflash or the official release process to flash the complete firmware image, which includes the partition table (partitions.csv). Do not flash only the application .bin.Full chip erase — Run espflash erase-flash before reflashing to start from a completely clean state.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and execution falls through — the WebSocket connection and normal operation continue. The OTA state may be left in an inconsistent state until the next reconnect cycle. The device will not reboot automatically.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The firmware download was corrupted (checksum/signature mismatch). This can happen if the WebSocket connection dropped mid-transfer.The firmware binary on the update server is itself corrupted.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Retry the OTA update — Trigger the update again from the FKMTime web interface. A successful update will complete verification correctly.Check server-side firmware binary — Confirm the binary hosted for updates is not corrupted (re-upload if necessary).Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if verification fails consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: bluetooth_loop returns. The outer bluetooth_timer_task retries the entire loop after a 1-second sleep. The error is recorded once per boot (subsequent failures in the same session do not add more entries). All other firmware tasks are unaffected.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged, the error log is saved to NVS, the display shows "Connection lost / during update", and the device reboots after 5 seconds. The bootloader will attempt to boot the last valid firmware slot (the update did not complete).

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Wi-Fi signal dropped during the update.The FKMTime server restarted or lost connectivity mid-transfer.Network congestion caused the WebSocket to time out.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait for the device to reboot — It will come back up on the previous firmware automatically. Confirm normal operation before attempting the update again.Improve Wi-Fi conditions — Move the device closer to the access point and retry the update when the connection is stable.Retry the OTA update — Trigger it again from the FKMTime web interface once the device is back online.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and boot continues normally. The failure is non-fatal for the current session. However, because the OTA slot was not marked valid, the bootloader may roll back to the previous firmware on the next reboot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: A flash write error occurred while marking the slot (worn flash cell, brief power interruption).The OTA state partition is corrupted.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Trigger another OTA update — A successful update will correctly mark the new slot as valid.Reflash via USB — Connect the device via USB and use espflash to flash the firmware directly. This bypasses OTA and resets the OTA state.Contact support — If this error appears after every OTA update, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: A transient failure bringing up the BLE radio — this is more likely after a watchdog reset or an ungraceful reboot.The BLE radio is in a bad state from a previous session.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait — The BLE task retries automatically every second. In most cases it recovers on the next attempt.Reboot the device — A clean power cycle resets the BLE radio state.Contact support — If BLE never recovers across multiple reboots, open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: rfid_task exits immediately. RFID scanning is unavailable for this session. All other firmware tasks continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Heap memory exhaustion at startup prevented the DMA buffer allocation.A firmware bug or corrupted build produced an invalid DMA configuration.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — Frees memory and retries.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware using espflash with a full chip erase.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this recurs consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The scan arm of the BLE discovery select4 returns early. The rest of the select4 logic runs (the device may still proceed toward a connect attempt, but without active scanning). The error is recorded once per boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The BLE controller entered an unexpected state preventing a new scan from starting.A transient radio driver error.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — Resets the BLE controller state.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The current iteration of bluetooth_loop's inner loop continues — the loop retries immediately. The error is recorded once per boot. BLE scanning and connection attempts continue on the next loop iteration.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The eFuse MAC address could not be converted to the expected 6-byte format. This is extremely unlikely on functioning hardware and may indicate a driver or firmware bug.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait / reboot — The loop retries automatically.Contact support — If this error appears consistently, open an issue on GitHub with your firmware version and device model.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The inner loop breaks and bluetooth_loop returns. The outer bluetooth_timer_task retries after 1 second. The error is recorded once per boot. BLE connection to the FKMTime Display is unavailable until the retry succeeds or the bond data is cleared.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The bond data stored in NVS is corrupted or in a format the current BLE stack cannot parse.A firmware update changed the bond data format.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Clear the stored BLE bond — Use the device's bond-clear option in the settings menu. This removes the corrupted bond from NVS, allowing a fresh pairing.Re-pair with the FKMTime Display — After clearing, pair again through the BLE pairing menu.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if clearing the bond does not resolve the issue.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The current connection attempt is abandoned (continue 'outer) and the device retries the connection loop immediately. The error is recorded once per boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The BLE stack rejected the bondable flag, possibly because the connection state changed between being established and this call.A transient stack state issue.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait — The outer connection loop retries automatically.Reboot the device — Resets all BLE state.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this recurs consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The current connection attempt is abandoned (continue 'outer) and the device retries the connection loop immediately. The error is recorded once per boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The BLE stack rejected the security request — this can happen if the connection dropped at the exact moment the request was made.The FKMTime Display rejected the security request.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait — The connection loop retries automatically.Clear the bond and re-pair — If this error appears repeatedly, delete the stored bond and pair the FKMTime Display again from scratch.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The write_fut future returns. The device disconnects and the outer connection loop retries. The error is recorded once per boot. The firmware looks for characteristic UUID a5178cad-e4e0-4598-8053-a4a78b9281e2.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The service was found but the specific characteristic is missing — the FKMTime Display firmware likely has a different GATT layout than expected.The connected device has a partial or non-standard GATT profile.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Update both firmware versions — Ensure both devices are on the latest firmware to keep their GATT profiles in sync.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub with the FKMTime Display firmware version. Include whether E58 also appears.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The inner pairing event loop breaks. The outer connection loop ('outer) continues, which means the device will attempt to reconnect and pair again. The error is recorded once per boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The FKMTime Display rejected the pairing request (e.g., it is bonded to another device and rejected a new bond).RF interference corrupted the BLE key exchange.The FKMTime Display firmware version is incompatible with the device firmware.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Clear bonds on both sides — Delete the bond from the FKMTime device (settings menu) and from the FKMTime Display. Then re-pair.Retry pairing — Move both devices close together in a low-interference environment and retry from the BLE pairing menu.Update firmware — Ensure both devices are on the latest firmware.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The current connection attempt is abandoned (continue 'outer) and the device retries the connection loop. The error is recorded once per boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Not enough BLE stack resources to create the GATT client.The connection dropped between being established and the GATT client creation.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait — The device retries the connection automatically.Reboot the device — Frees all BLE stack resources for a clean start.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The write_fut future returns. The device disconnects and the outer connection loop retries. The error is recorded once per boot. The firmware looks for service UUID a5bad9f2-700a-4c3d-b9e2-e58ad262d40e.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The connected BLE device does not expose the expected service — it may not be a FKMTime Display, or may be running incompatible firmware.The FKMTime Display firmware was updated and changed its service UUID.GATT service discovery timed out (5-second timeout) before the service list was returned.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Verify the connected device — Confirm you are pairing with a FKMTime Display running compatible firmware.Update both firmware versions — Ensure both devices are on the latest firmware.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub with the FKMTime Display firmware version.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged, the error log is saved to NVS, and the device reboots after 1 second. The device cannot operate without a Wi-Fi connection, so a reboot is the only path forward.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Wi-Fi credentials stored in NVS are wrong or have been corrupted — the device cannot connect to the configured access point.The configured Wi-Fi network is out of range or down.NVS data is corrupted and the Wi-Fi manager cannot parse its configuration.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Verify the Wi-Fi network is available — Confirm the access point is powered on and in range.Reconfigure Wi-Fi credentials — If the device cannot connect with its stored credentials, hold the configuration button to enter setup mode and re-enter the correct SSID and password.Erase NVS and reflash — If credentials are corrupted beyond recovery, perform a full flash erase (espflash erase-flash) and reflash. You will need to reconfigure Wi-Fi from scratch.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged, the error log is saved to NVS, the stored Wi-Fi configuration is deleted from NVS (WIFI_NVS_KEY), and the device reboots after 1 second. On the next boot, the device will enter Wi-Fi setup mode because its credentials have been erased.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The FKMTime server is not running or not advertising an mDNS service on the network.Another device on the network is advertising an mDNS service with the same name as FKMTime, returning a malformed or unexpected response.The FKMTime server version is incompatible with the device firmware and uses a different URL format.The network blocks mDNS traffic (common on enterprise/managed networks).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Ensure the FKMTime server is running — Confirm the server process is active and reachable on the same local network.Check for mDNS conflicts — Make sure no other device is advertising the same mDNS service name.Reconfigure Wi-Fi — Since credentials are erased on this error, enter setup mode after the reboot and re-enter Wi-Fi credentials. The device will attempt mDNS discovery again on the next connection.Check network mDNS support — On networks that block mDNS, configure the device to use a static server URL instead.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot, ws_loop returns an error, and the outer ws_task loop waits 500 ms before calling ws_loop again. The device retries the connection automatically.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The server closed the TCP connection immediately, possibly because the request path, version query parameters, or authentication did not match what the server expects.The server is running but not at the path the device is connecting to (version mismatch between device firmware and server).A firewall, reverse proxy, or load balancer is terminating the connection before the server sees it.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Check server and firmware versions — Ensure the FKMTime server and device firmware are on compatible versions.Check server logs — Look for rejected connection attempts around the time this error occurred.Check network path — If a reverse proxy is in use, ensure it passes WebSocket upgrade requests through without terminating them.Wait — The device retries automatically. If the server was momentarily restarting, it will reconnect once the server is back.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: When the server sends back card info and the solve is in the Finished state, the firmware checks that a solve group is set in the device state. If it is None, this error is logged once (per boot) and the solve submission is silently skipped. The RFID scanning loop continues running — the device can still scan cards, but this particular solve is lost.  This is an unexpected edge case that should not occur under normal circumstances.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The device connected to the server before its station assignment was fully loaded into its state. This can happen if the server sends card data immediately after connection before the solve group has been synchronised.The device's station assignment was removed in the FKMTime web interface while it was running.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Verify station assignment — In the FKMTime web interface, go to Devices and confirm this device is assigned to a station.Reboot the device — A fresh connection to the server will resynchronise the solve group.Contact support — If this error appears during normal competition operation, open an issue on GitHub and attach the micro-connector logs.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The bad message is dropped and the WS read loop continues — the device keeps reading subsequent messages normally. The error is logged once per boot. No reconnect or reboot occurs.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The server sent a message that uses a different JSON schema than the firmware expects — typically a version mismatch between server and device firmware.A network corruption event mangled the payload (very unlikely on a local TCP connection).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Update both server and firmware — The most common cause is a version mismatch. Update the FKMTime server and device firmware to compatible versions.Check server logs — Look for error messages around the time the bad packet was sent.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The packet is silently dropped — it is never sent to the server. The error is logged once per boot. The WebSocket connection and all other operations continue normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: Heap allocation failed during JSON serialisation. This can happen if the heap is severely fragmented after a long session or after recovering from a crash.A firmware bug caused invalid data to be placed in the packet fields (e.g., a non-finite float).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — Resets the heap. If this was a one-off allocation failure it will not recur.Update the firmware — Newer firmware may reduce peak heap usage during serialisation.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently, especially if it coincides with missing solve submissions.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot (subsequent failures in the same session are silently retried), the connection loop waits 1 second, and then retries the DNS lookup and WebSocket connection. The device keeps retrying indefinitely until it resolves the server address.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The FKMTime server is not running or its mDNS advertisement has stopped.The device's DNS resolver cannot reach the server — common on networks that do not support mDNS passthrough.The device joined a different Wi-Fi network than the one the server is on.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Verify the FKMTime server is running — Check the server process on the host machine.Check the Wi-Fi network — Ensure the device and server are on the same local network (not separated by VLANs or guest network isolation).Test mDNS on the network — Use an mDNS browser (e.g. Discovery - DNS-SD Browser on macOS/iOS, or avahi-browse -a on Linux) to check whether the FKMTime service is visible on the network.Configure a static server URL — If mDNS is unavailable, configure the device with the server's IP address directly.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot and the caller continues. The in-memory state is unaffected — the device keeps running normally. However, the state that should have been persisted (e.g., current session, competitor info) will not survive a reboot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The NVS partition is full.A flash write error (worn cell, brief power interruption during write).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — A fresh boot retries.Erase NVS and reflash — If NVS is consistently failing to write, perform a full flash erase (espflash erase-flash) and reflash. All stored settings will be lost.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and the function returns. The bond is active in RAM for the current session — the FKMTime Display will keep working until the device reboots. After a reboot, the bond is lost and the devices will need to re-pair.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The NVS partition is full.A flash write error.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Re-pair after the next reboot — If the bond is lost on reboot, go to the BLE pairing menu and pair again. The new pairing attempt may write successfully if NVS space has been freed.Erase NVS and reflash — If NVS writes consistently fail, perform a full flash erase and reflash.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot, the task waits 500 ms, and then retries getting the subscriber in a loop. Requests that require a tagged response (e.g., solve submissions) are blocked until a subscriber is available. The WebSocket connection itself is not affected.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: All subscriber slots on the TAGGED_RETURN PubSubChannel are occupied — too many concurrent requests are waiting for responses simultaneously.A firmware bug caused the channel to reach its subscriber limit.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Wait — The retry loop resolves this automatically once a subscriber slot becomes free.Reboot the device — Resets all channel state.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently during normal competition use.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot and the caller continues. The stale NVS entry remains and may be loaded on the next boot.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The NVS partition is corrupted and cannot process delete operations.The entry did not exist in NVS, but the delete operation still returned an error.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot. The menu still closes and the new volume is applied in RAM for the current session. After a reboot, the volume will revert to the previously saved value (or the default if nothing was saved).

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The NVS partition is full.A flash write error.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Retry changing the volume — After a reboot, try setting the volume again. A transient write error may not recur.Erase NVS and reflash — If NVS writes consistently fail, perform a full flash erase and reflash.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — The stale state may be handled gracefully on the next boot and the delete retried.Erase NVS and reflash — A full flash erase removes all NVS entries including the stuck one.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub if this appears consistently.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged once per boot, error_log_entries is set to an empty list, and the device proceeds to show the error log menu with no entries. This is non-critical — the device otherwise continues normally.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The error log was written by an incompatible older firmware version using a different binary format.The NVS entry containing the log is corrupted (e.g., a partial write from a crash during log saving).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: No action needed in most cases — The device ignores the unparseable log and continues normally. The corrupt entry will be overwritten next time an error is logged.Erase NVS and reflash — If this error appears on every boot and is accompanied by other NVS failures, a full flash erase may help.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged (blocking block_on) and spawn_task returns. The task that failed to spawn never runs — whatever functionality it provides (RFID, display, BLE, Stackmat, battery, etc.) is absent for the session. The rest of the firmware continues.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: The task pool for that task type is exhausted — the same task was already spawned elsewhere and Embassy does not allow duplicate instances of the same #[embassy_executor::task].A firmware bug or corrupted build caused the spawn token to be invalid.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Reboot the device — A fresh boot clears all task state.Reflash the firmware — Flash the latest firmware with espflash to rule out a corrupted build.Contact support — Open an issue on GitHub and note which functionality is missing (which subsystem is not working), as that will identify which task failed.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: When the device panics, custom_pre_backtrace sets an RTC RAM flag (NVS_PANIC_MAGIC_1). If the device panics again before a clean boot clears this flag, the flag becomes NVS_PANIC_MAGIC_2. On the next boot, verify_panic_flag detects the double-panic and:  Logs E90 (blocking).Reads the backtrace length from the end of the NVS flash region.Erases the NVS partition to allow recovery — this deletes all saved settings (Wi-Fi credentials, BLE bonds, saved state, error log, etc.). If a valid backtrace is stored, only the portion before it is erased to preserve crash info; otherwise the full NVS region is erased.Clears the panic flag.Boot continues normally — there is no halt.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: A reproducible firmware bug that crashes the device on every boot.Corrupted NVS data causing a crash on boot when the state is read.A hardware fault triggering a consistent crash (power brownout, etc.).

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Check if the device recovered — After two panics the device erases the NVS partition and attempts a normal boot. It may recover on its own, but all saved settings are gone — you will need to reconfigure Wi-Fi credentials and re-pair any BLE devices.Erase NVS and reflash — Perform a full flash erase (espflash erase-flash) and reflash to clear all corrupted state.Report the issue — E90 always indicates a crash loop that needs investigation. Open an issue on GitHub with the firmware version and as much context as possible about what the device was doing before it started crashing.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and the timed-out transaction is abandoned. The affected peripheral may miss an operation for that cycle (e.g. a skipped battery read, a dropped display frame, or a failed RFID poll). The firmware continues and retries on subsequent cycles. If timeouts recur, multiple subsystems may appear degraded at once.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: A peripheral on the shared I²C bus is not responding or is holding the bus line low.Loose or faulty cabling to the display or another I²C device.Electrical noise or a short on the I²C lines.The battery was disconnected, causing the fuel gauge to stop responding.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: Check physical connections — Reseat the display cable and ensure the battery is connected, then reboot.Reboot the device — Clears a stuck bus state and reinitialises all peripherals.Note which features are affected — If only the display fails, suspect the OLED cable; if battery percentage is also stale, the issue may be bus-wide.Contact support — If this error appears frequently after checking connections, open an issue on GitHub and note which subsystems are affected.

searchDocs.title: What happens​
searchDocs.content: The error is logged and read_saved_backtrace returns early — no stacktrace is added to the error log. Boot continues normally. This error appears in two contexts:  During verify_panic_flag (release builds, after a double-panic): the backtrace length could not be read from flash. The NVS region may still be partially erased for recovery.During read_saved_backtrace: called after Wi-Fi connects; the backtrace from the previous crash session could not be read from its location in flash.

searchDocs.title: Possible causes​
searchDocs.content: A flash read error at the backtrace storage location (end of the NVS partition).The backtrace was never written (the crash handler itself failed before saving it).The NVS partition boundary calculation was wrong.

searchDocs.title: How to fix​
searchDocs.content: No immediate action needed — The device boots normally. The lost backtrace means the crash that caused the previous panic cannot be symbolised, but the device itself is operational.Report the crash — If E91 is accompanied by a previous panic (look for a Panic entry in the error log), open an issue on GitHub with your firmware version and a description of what happened before the crash.

searchDocs.title: Install the Rust ESP toolchain​
searchDocs.content: The firmware is built on top of esp-hal (Rust). First, set up the Rust ESP toolchain by following the official installation guide.  Then install espflash, which is used as the Cargo runner to flash and monitor the device.

searchDocs.title: Building & Running​
searchDocs.content: Once the toolchain is installed, you can build and flash the firmware with a single command.  git clone https://github.com/FKMTime/firmware cd firmware cargo run -r   cargo run -r builds the firmware for the v4 board in release mode and flashes it to the connected device using espflash (configured as the Cargo runner). For a v3 board, add --no-default-features --features v3.  By default after build, binaries are also copied into /tmp/fkm-build folder. Development binaries are marked with their build time (epoch seconds).

searchDocs.title: Flashing​
searchDocs.content: To flash a built firmware binary onto a connected device manually, use espflash. For day-to-day development simply running cargo run -r in the firmware repository will build and flash the device in one step.  For over-the-air updates you can use the built-in OTA (over the air update) in the micro-connector.  By default micro-connector is watching /tmp/fkm-build dir for firmware changes.  To flash development firmware you need to set the DEV environment variable for micro-connector. If you are running micro-connector using cargo (not docker) you can set it in the .env file in its project dir.

searchDocs.title: Common issues​
searchDocs.content: If you aren't using DEV mode your firmware won't be updated to the development version of firmware.

searchDocs.title: Importing database dump
searchDocs.content: Importing database dump You can import the database dump into the development environmentin the following way. Run the commands in the root directory of the FKMTime repository, with the dev stack running. Clear the development database: docker compose exec database psql -d fkm_time -c 'DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;' Import the dump: docker compose exec -T database psql -d fkm_time < dump.sql Restart the backend, so it brings the schema up to date: docker compose restart backend That's it! You have successfully imported the database dump into the development environment.

searchDocs.title: Using the dev stack​
searchDocs.content: The dev stack in the FKMTime repository already runs the micro-connector (the micro_connector service, using the published image), so you don't need to set it up separately unless you are working on the micro-connector itself. On macOS, start theBluetooth adapter first.

searchDocs.title: Running micro-connector from source​
searchDocs.content: Clone micro-connector repo and navigate into it  git clone https://github.com/FKMTime/micro-connector cd micro-connector   Requirements​  Rust (1.85 or later, the crate uses the 2024 edition)Cargo  Copy .env.example to .env and adjust it. SOCKET_PATH must point to the backend's unix socket, and FIRMWARE_DIR is the folder watched fordevelopment firmware. NO_BT=1 turns off Bluetooth and NO_MDNS=1 turns off mDNS.  cp .env.example .env   Then run  cargo run   To see logs for the micro-connector only, use:  RUST_LOG=none,backend=trace cargo run   note Stop the micro_connector service of the dev stack first (docker compose stop micro_connector): only one micro-connector per machine can run at a time.

searchDocs.title: Docker​
searchDocs.content: The dev stack in docker-compose.yml runs the backend, frontend, PostgreSQL,dummy WCA and dummy WCA Live and themicro-connector. Run the following commands in the root directory of the project:  docker compose pull dummy_wca dummy_wca_live micro_connector docker compose up -d --build   Then seed the database with a sample competition:  docker compose exec backend npx ts-node prisma/seed/seed-test.ts   The seed imports the competition that the dummy WCA generates (invented people, a two-day schedule starting today), so it needs the dummy WCA running. It also creates an account with username admin and password admin, which you can use to sign in instead of a WCA account.  What	WherePanel	http://localhost:5173 Backend	http://localhost:5000 (/health) Station tester	http://localhost:5173/station-tester Database	localhost:5433 (user root, password password, database fkm_time) Dummy WCA / WCA Live	http://localhost:3005 / http://localhost:4000  Backend and frontend source code is mounted into the containers, so changes reload on their own. Rebuild (docker compose up -d --build) after changing dependencies.  tip If you are not working on anything that needs a real device, you can skip the micro-connector: put FKMTIME_MICRO_CONNECTOR=0 in .env in the project root and leave micro_connector out of the pull. The station tester covers station messages without one.

searchDocs.title: Bluetooth on macOS​
searchDocs.content: The micro-connector uses Linux D-Bus for Bluetooth, which containers on macOS cannot reach. Run docker-adapternatively instead:  ./scripts/docker-adapter.sh   The script downloads the adapter on first run. Keep it running, and allow Bluetooth for your terminal in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Bluetooth. Start the adapter before docker compose up: the micro-connector looks for it only at startup. If the stack is already running, restart it with docker compose restart micro_connector.  warning Keep the backend in Docker when you work with devices. The micro-connector talks to the backend over a unix socket in a Docker volume, and a unix socket can't cross into the Docker VM on macOS.

searchDocs.title: Several stacks on one machine​
searchDocs.content: Each clone (or git worktree) is its own Docker Compose project with its own database. To run a second one next to the first, run ./scripts/dev-ports.shbefore docker compose up. It picks free ports, writes them to .env and prints the URLs; ./scripts/dev-ports.sh --clear goes back to the defaults. Only one stack per machine can run the micro-connector, so dev-ports.shturns it off in the stack it sets up.  ./scripts/dev-teardown.sh removes the stack of the current directory for good: containers, volumes (its database too), images and the ports in .env.

searchDocs.title: Running backend and frontend separately​
searchDocs.content: Requirements​  Node.js (current LTS)PostgreSQLDummy WCA and dummy WCA Live (or real WCA servers)  Setup database​  Install PostgreSQLCreate a database  CREATE DATABASE fkm_time;   Backend​  Navigate into backend directory  cd backend   Install dependencies  npm install   Create .env file and enter database URL, secret (at least 32 characters), and WCA and WCA Live URLs  DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@localhost:5432/fkm_time SECRET=dev-only-secret-not-for-production-change-me WCA_LIVE_API_ORIGIN=http://localhost:4000/api WCA_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3005 WCA_CLIENT_ID=example-application-id WCA_CLIENT_SECRET=example-secret   Create the database tables  npx prisma db push   Seed the database with sample data (needs the dummy WCA running atWCA_ORIGIN)  npx ts-node prisma/seed/seed-test.ts   This will also create a user with username admin and password admin, you can use these credentials to login to the admin panel instead of WCA account.  Run backend in development mode  npm run start:dev   The server will be accessible at localhost:5000  Frontend​  Navigate into frontend directory  cd frontend   Install dependencies  npm install   Run development server  npm run dev   Admin panel will be accessible at localhost:5173. Set VITE_BACKEND_ORIGINand VITE_WCA_ORIGIN if your backend or WCA server runs somewhere other thanhttp://localhost:5000 and the WCA staging server.  note Always use Vite's dev server (npm run dev), not vite preview: a production build ignores VITE_BACKEND_ORIGIN and VITE_WCA_ORIGIN.

searchDocs.title: WCA website​
searchDocs.content: By default, FKMTime uses dummy-wca, which is included in the docker-compose.yml file (at http://localhost:3005). With this as a WCA server, you can sign in with OAuth by choosing one of its accounts, and import competition.  Besides a few snapshot competitions, dummy-wca serves a generated test competition (invented people, a two-day schedule starting the day the server starts) and emulates WCA integrated live results for it. Open http://localhost:3005 to see every competition it knows and to generate new ones.  If you want to use real WCA Server you can either setup local WCA Server or use a staging one (if you have access). If you want to use staging server just change WCA_ORIGIN of the backend in docker-compose.yml to https://staging.worldcubeassociation.org, and VITE_WCA_ORIGIN of the frontend to the same address.

searchDocs.title: WCA Live​
searchDocs.content: By default FKMTime uses dummy-wca-live, which is included in the docker-compose.yml file (at http://localhost:4000). It accepts results like the real WCA Live API. Set the scoretaking token to wca-live-token and this server will behave like real WCA Live server.  You can read how to setup local WCA Live server here

searchDocs.title: Open​
searchDocs.content: Open lists every incident waiting for a decision: the competitor, the round, the attempt number, the station, the judge, the time and how long ago it was solved. Click an incident to open it next to the list.    The incident shows:  Previous extras - the competitor's earlier incidents in the competition, grouped by comment, so you can see if the same thing keeps happeningQuick actions - one click resolves the incident with a ready comment. The built-in ones (A7G, Judge fault, Distraction, Timer malfunction) give an extra attempt; you can add your own (see Quick actions). A quick action saves the attempt as the station sent it and ignores the form below; to correct the time, penalty or judge, edit the form and use Mark as resolved or Save and give extra insteadInspection time, as measured by the stationAttempt number, Time, Penalty and Judge - correct them if the station got something wrongComment - why you decided what you did; it shows in the Resolved tab and in the SummaryMark as noteworthy incident - also saves the incident to the Noteworthy tabDo not require cards to be scanned (bugs only) - normally, after Mark as resolved, the station asks for the competitor's and judge's cards again to confirm the result. Tick this only when the station can't get past that step  Then choose:  Mark as resolved - the attempt counts with the time and penalty in the form. If the time is over the round's time limit, it's changed to DNFSave and give extra - the competitor gets an extra attempt in place of this oneDelete attempt - removes the attempt completely, after you confirm  Your answer goes back to the station straight away. Unless you gave an extra, the result is sent to the results website.  When several attempts of a competitor are affected, follow Several attempts affected? Give extras on the result page to give the extras on the result's page.

searchDocs.title: Tutorial incidents​
searchDocs.content: When a station runs the tutorial for new competitors, its delegate calls show up in Open too, marked Tutorial. You answer them with the same quick actions, Time, Penalty, Mark as resolved, Give extra or Delete, but nothing is saved: the answer only goes back to the station. Tutorial incidents are for delegates only.

searchDocs.title: Resolved​
searchDocs.content: Resolved has every incident that was already decided: competitor, round, attempt, time, when it was solved, who resolved it (By), the outcome (Status), comment and judge. Use the search to find a competitor.    Each row has:  View attempts - opens the competitor's result in that roundCopy incident info - copies the competitor, their WCA ID and the round and attempt (e.g. 2x2 R1A2), for a delegate reportSave as noteworthy - adds the incident to the Noteworthy tab  Summary groups the resolved incidents by comment and shows for each one whether an extra was given, the attempt was a DNF, or the original time stands.

searchDocs.title: Noteworthy​
searchDocs.content: Noteworthy collects incidents worth mentioning in the delegate report. An incident marked as noteworthy is added here with the competitor and round as its title and the incident's comment as its description; you can also click Add noteworthy incident and write one yourself (Title and Description). Each one can be edited or deleted, and one saved from an attempt has View attempts.

searchDocs.title: Warnings​
searchDocs.content: Warnings lists the warnings given to competitors and who gave them. Click Add warning, choose the Competitor and describe what happened. You can also give a warning with Issue warning on the Persons page or on the Attendance page.

searchDocs.title: Manual​
searchDocs.content: Manual is for incidents that didn't come from a station. Click Add manual incident and fill in Competitor, Event, Round, Attempt and Description. Manual incidents can be edited or deleted.  If the competition doesn't use FKMTime devices, this is where Incidents opens.

searchDocs.title: Quick actions​
searchDocs.content: Besides the built-in quick actions, each delegate can add their own in Settings → Quick actions.    Click Add quick action and fill in:  Name - the button's label in an incidentComment - saved as the incident's commentGive extra attempt - ticked, the action gives an extra; unticked, it resolves the incident and the time standsShare with other delegates - other delegates of the competition see the action too. Unshared, only you do    The list shows what each action does (Gives extra or Resolves, no extra) and whether it's Shared or Only me. Each action can be edited, shared or unshared, or deleted.

searchDocs.title: Double check​
searchDocs.content: Type the competitor's ID from the scorecard into Competitor ID (or pick them from the list next to it). Their result opens on the right: average, best, the time limit and cutoff, and each attempt with its Time, Penalty and the Final result.Compare it with the scorecard. If something differs, correct the time or penalty right there. A time over the time limit becomes DNF.Press Enter (or Confirm) to mark the result as double-checked. FKMTime saves it and sends it to the results website again; if you changed anything, it asks first.Type the next ID.    Skip leaves a result for later. Details opens the result, for anything you can't fix in the list (see A single result).The progress shows how many results are double-checked and how many are not finished: results still missing attempts or with an open incident. They can be double-checked once they're complete.Missing competitors lists the competitors of the round with no result yet.Open incidents in this round lists the round's incidents, each linking to the incident.A scorecard that was already double-checked says so when you type its ID.  When every result is double-checked, the page says All N results double-checked. Mark results as not double checked starts the round over.

searchDocs.title: Enter scorecard​
searchDocs.content: Use Enter scorecard when attempts were written only on paper, for example when a station didn't work.  Type the competitor's ID into Competitor (or pick them from the list). Their scorecard opens with every attempt of the round; attempts already in FKMTime are filled in. Press Enter to jump to the first time.Type each Time and choose its Penalty. A time over the time limit becomes DNF.Press Enter in the last time, or click Save scorecard. FKMTime confirms with Saved … scorecard and a link to Open result, and the cursor goes back to Competitor for the next one.    Details opens the competitor's result. If the competitor is waiting for an extra attempt, the scorecard can't be entered here; enter the attempts on their result instead.

searchDocs.title: Opening a group​
searchDocs.content: Open Attendance from the menu, or click Attendance on a room's card on the Home page. If exactly one room is running a group, the page opens on that group.  Choose a round from the strip at the top (rounds in progress show Live), or from the round list on its left (Choose a round). On a phone, pick the event and then the round instead. Then pick the group. A dot marks the group in progress. Previous group and Next group (the arrows on both sides) go through every group in schedule order, across rounds.    Above the cards you see how many people are present and absent in the group. The Competitors, Scramblers, Runners and Judges buttons show or hide each card. Your choice is remembered on this device. A role with nobody in the group stays hidden until you turn it on.  Each card shows how many people are present out of everyone in that role (e.g. 4/8), and splits them into Absent and Present. The page updates live when someone else marks a person or a station checks a competitor in.

searchDocs.title: Taking attendance for staff​
searchDocs.content: For an absent scrambler, runner or judge, click Mark present (the tick). The menu (⋮) next to them has:  Mark late - they did the job, but came lateReplaced… - someone else did the job (see below)Not coming today - see Not coming todayComment - a note on this assignmentIssue warning - delegates only    When a card has more than one absent person, Mark all present marks all of them at once.  For someone present, the menu has Left early (only for present or late; it reads Didn't leave early once set), Comment, Issue warning (delegates only) and Mark absent. Marking absent someone who wasn't assigned to the group removes them from the list, after you confirm.  After you mark someone, a message with Undo shows for a few seconds. Undo puts that person back as they were. Undoing Replaced… doesn't remove the person who did the job; mark them absent if they shouldn't be there. Removing someone who wasn't assigned can't be undone.

searchDocs.title: Replaced​
searchDocs.content: Replaced… asks who did the job instead. Pick the person, or leave it empty if you don't know. Then click:  They were here - the person came, but someone else did the job,They didn't come - the person stays absent, and the row shows Covered by the person who did it.  The person who did the job is added as present if they aren't yet, and their row shows Covering for.

searchDocs.title: Badges​
searchDocs.content: Rows show what applies to them: Late, Left early, Replaced / Replaced by, Covered by, Covering for, Unassigned (present without an assignment) and Not coming.

searchDocs.title: Not coming today​
searchDocs.content: When you hear that a staff member isn't coming, for example they're ill, choose Not coming today on one of their absent rows. FKMTime marks them as not coming in that group and in every group of theirs later that day that hasn't ended yet. Groups that are over keep what was recorded. Their rows show Not coming and drop to the bottom of the Absent list, so the people still expected stay on top.  Coming after all undoes it. Marking them present, or scanning their card, clears it for that group.  You can do the same from a person's page, next to each day of their schedule. A stage leader can mark someone as not coming if one of that person's groups that day is in their rooms; it applies to the whole day.

searchDocs.title: Adding someone who wasn't assigned​
searchDocs.content: To add a scrambler, runner or judge who wasn't assigned to the group, click the person icon in the card's header, pick the person and click Add and mark as present. If they compete in this group, FKMTime warns you and the button reads Add anyway.

searchDocs.title: Judges at stations​
searchDocs.content: A judge is marked present automatically when they sign an attempt with their card on a station in that group. If they weren't assigned, they're added as an unassigned judge. Once runners are assigned for the round, present judges show their station (e.g. · Station 3).  Scramblers and runners can also check in on an attendance device by tapping their card.

searchDocs.title: Competitors​
searchDocs.content: A competitor is marked present when an attempt of theirs in the group is entered, from a station or from the panel. You can't mark competitors present by hand.  In a later round, every competitor shows their place in the previous round in brackets, e.g. (3), so you can tell whether a missing competitor matters.  For an absent competitor:  Change group (the arrows) moves them to another group of the same round. Pick New group, click Submit and confirm. The change is written to the competition on the WCA website, and any other assignment they have during the new group is deleted. Only organizers and delegates who signed in with a WCA account can do it.Not coming marks them as not coming to this group only. FKMTime then doesn't wait for them before changing the group automatically. Coming after all undoes it, and an attempt from them clears it.Remove from round - organizers and delegates, in a later round, when the competition sends results to WCA Integrated Live Results and FKMTime is connected to it. If the round isn't open there yet, FKMTime offers to open it first (Open … first). Then it asks the WCA who is next in line, and you choose whether they advance.

searchDocs.title: Most missed​
searchDocs.content: The Most missed tab lists everyone in the competition, with those who missed the most staff assignments first. Competing doesn't count. Only groups that have started count as missed. Not coming assignments show even for groups still ahead.  Filter the list with All, Missed, Not coming, Late, Left early and Replaced. Click a person to see the groups behind each count and the comments on their assignments. Groups shows their assignments; delegates also have Warnings and Issue warning.

searchDocs.title: Statistics​
searchDocs.content: The Statistics tab shows staff attendance for the whole competition, counting only groups that have started.    Cards at the top: Attendance (the share of assignments covered), Late (counted as attended), Absent (with how many are not coming for the day), Replaced, Left early and Extra help (people who helped without an assignment).By round - attendance per round.The table, one row per person, with columns Name, Attendance, Assigned, Present, Late, Absent, Replaced, Left early, No-show and Extra help. Click a column header to sort by it.  When more than one role has staff, choose a role at the top (All roles, Judge, Scrambler, Runner…) to see the numbers for that role only. Use the search box to find someone in the table.

searchDocs.title: Giving delegate access​
searchDocs.content: You can give access from three places. Each opens the same Give delegate access dialog:  Incidents → Delegate access tab → Give delegate access - for any group running now or any room's next groupHome → the room's More (…) menu → Give delegate access… - for the room's running and next groupsSetup → Users → the user's row menu → Give delegate access… - with the user already chosen. It shows only for users who aren't delegates or admins  On Home, a No delegate free for… alert appears when every delegate of the competition competes in a running or next group. Its Give delegate access… button opens the dialog for that group. The alert goes away once someone has access for the group.  In the dialog, choose the User and the Group, tick what they can do besides resolving incidents, and click Give access.

searchDocs.title: What they can do​
searchDocs.content: Delegate access always includes resolving incidents: correcting the time, penalty, judge and comment of an incident and clicking Mark as resolved. Under Besides resolving incidents, they can, you choose the rest:  Option	Ticked by defaultGive an extra	Yes Add an attempt	Yes Reorder attempts	Yes Edit an attempt that isn't an incident	No Delete an attempt	No Give extras for several attempts	No DNF all attempts	No  Whatever you tick, they can only act on competitors of that group: those assigned to it, and those who solved in it on a station in the room that runs it. Delegate access never includes removing a result, double-checking, sending or resubmitting results, restarting a group or assigning DNS, and never the Resolved, Noteworthy, Warnings, Manual or Delegate access tabs. A DNF all attempts that would also remove results from later rounds is refused.  Giving access again to the same user for the same group changes the options of the access they already have.

searchDocs.title: When it starts and ends​
searchDocs.content: Given for a group that is running, access works straight away.Given for a room's next group, it waits (Starts with the group) and starts when a room starts the group.It ends by itself when the group stops running, for example when the room moves to the next group. Ended access never comes back, even if the group is started again; give access again if needed.To end it early, click End on the Delegate access tab and confirm with End access.

searchDocs.title: What they did​
searchDocs.content: The Delegate access tab lists the access that hasn't ended, then the access that ended today.
