Each row shows the user, the group, its state (Active, Starts with the group or Ended), what it allows and who gave and ended it.    Click the number of actions (for example 3 actions) to see what the user did: the time, the competitor (linking to their result) and what changed. The list updates live, so you can look over their decisions while the group runs.

searchDocs.title: What the user with access sees​
searchDocs.content: A banner across the panel says which group the access is for and who gave it, and whether it Starts when the group starts or Ends when the group ends. When the access ends, the banner says so for a few seconds.    They get Incidents in the menu with only the Open tab, showing the open incidents of their group. Buttons for actions their access doesn't include are hidden, and Mark as noteworthy incident and Previous extras don't show. If their access ends while they are working, saving fails with a message that it has ended, and the incident stays open for delegates.

searchDocs.title: The persons list​
searchDocs.content: Use Search by name or WCA ID to find someone. Next to the search you can narrow the list down:  ID - the person's registrant IDCard - the ID of a card, to find out whose card it is (only when the competition uses FKMTime devices)Newcomers - only competitors without a WCA IDNot checked in - only people who haven't checked in yet  On a phone these sit under Filters, with Clear to remove them all.  The list shows each person's registrant ID, name, WCA ID (or Newcomer), country, gender and events, and whether they are Checked in. With FKMTime devices it also shows whether they have a Card and whether they Can compete.  When the competition uses FKMTime devices, the page has two tabs: All persons and Assign cards. Assigning cards and checking in are described in Assigning cards & check-in.

searchDocs.title: Actions in a row​
searchDocs.content: Each row has these actions, depending on your role:  Assign card - assign or change the person's card (only with FKMTime devices).Groups - the person's groups: each group, what they do in it, whether they were present and whether they are assigned to it. Stage leaders, organizers and delegates.Warnings - the warnings the person got and who issued them. Delegates only.Issue warning - write a Description and click Issue warning. Delegates only.  Groups, Warnings and Issue warning are only there for people from the WCA registration, not for people added in FKMTime.

searchDocs.title: Adding a person​
searchDocs.content: Organizers and delegates can add a staff member or a competitor who competes only in unofficial events with Add person (only with FKMTime devices). See Competition Volunteers.

searchDocs.title: A person's page​
searchDocs.content: Stage leaders, organizers and delegates can click a name in the list to open the person's page. It shows their registrant ID, WCA ID and country, and these tabs:  Tab	Who sees itSchedule	Everyone who can open the page Results	Everyone who can open the page, when the competition uses FKMTime devices Incidents	Delegates Warnings	Delegates

searchDocs.title: Schedule​
searchDocs.content: The Schedule tab lists the person's assignments, day by day: time, group, room and station, and their role (for example Competitor, Judge or Runner). The assignment taking place right now is highlighted.  Stage leaders, organizers and delegates also see the attendance taken on the Attendance page: Present, Late, Absent, Replaced (with who replaced them), Left early, or Not coming. Click a group's name to open its attendance. A stage leader can open only the groups in their rooms.  If someone tells you they won't come for the rest of a day, click Not coming next to that day. It marks all their remaining staff assignments that day as not coming, so you don't have to take their attendance group by group. If they show up after all, click Coming after all. Both show an Undo for a few seconds. The button is there only while the person still has staff assignments to come that day. A stage leader sees it only on days when the person has a group in their rooms (see Stage leaders and rooms).

searchDocs.title: Results​
searchDocs.content: The Results tab lists the person's results in every round: group, average, best and the attempts. On a computer, click a round to open its results.  Organizers and delegates can click View attempts to open the result with all its attempts. Delegates also have DNF all attempts in an event (for example DNF all attempts in 3x3x3 Cube) in the row's menu, for example when a competitor is disqualified from an event. You can't use it while the person has an open incident in that event: resolve the incidents first.

searchDocs.title: Incidents​
searchDocs.content: The Incidents tab (delegates) collects every incident related to the person:  Attempts - attempts with an incident, with the round, attempt number, judge, station and result, and whether the incident is Open, Resolved or Extra granted. Attempts the person judged are included as well, marked As judge. Click an attempt to review an open incident or to see the result of a closed one.Manual incidents - incidents entered by hand.Noteworthy - noteworthy incidents about the person.

searchDocs.title: Warnings​
searchDocs.content: The Warnings tab (delegates) lists the person's warnings, who issued them and when. Click Issue warning to give them a new one. To remove a warning, click Delete warning (the bin icon) in its row; you can Undo it for a few seconds.

searchDocs.title: Public display​
searchDocs.content: Who can use it: anyone, no account needed.  Click Public display at the bottom of the sign-in page, or open /public on your FKMTime address. Share that link with competitors, for example on a QR code at the venue.  The sidebar has two items:  Live solving - the station board, described below. When the stations span several rooms, you can pick one room or All rooms.Results - the results of every round. Rounds with a group in progress are listed under Results in the sidebar.  At the bottom of the sidebar, TV view opens the TV view and Staff sign in goes back to the sign-in page. On a phone the sidebar becomes two tabs, Live solving and Results, under the header.  The header shows Live while the page is connected, or Reconnecting when it lost the connection. Everything updates on its own, so there is no need to refresh.

searchDocs.title: Results​
searchDocs.content: Pick an event at the top. Events with a round in progress have a dot. When the event has more than one round, switch between them with the round buttons on the right; again, a dot marks the round in progress. Opening Results without picking anything shows the round in progress, or the first round when nothing is running.  Under the round's name you see its format, its status (In progress, the number of competitors, or Not started) and how many competitors advance. The table ranks everyone with their attempts, Average and Best; the top three are highlighted.

searchDocs.title: TV view​
searchDocs.content: Who can use it: anyone, no account needed.  The TV view is made for a projector or a TV at the venue. Open TV view from the public display, or /public/tv directly, and click Fullscreen.  It rotates on its own, every 15 seconds, between:  Live solving - the station board for all roomsthe results of each round in progress - the top 10, with their attempts and their average (or best, depending on the format)  The dots next to the clock show which slide is on screen. There is nothing to click: the Fullscreen button and the mouse cursor hide after a few seconds without mouse movement, and the page keeps the screen from going to sleep. If you have a keyboard at hand, the left and right arrow keys switch slides.  If the connection drops, a Reconnecting badge says when the screen was last updated.

searchDocs.title: The station board​
searchDocs.content: Live solving shows one card per station, grouped by room. Next to each room's name you see the round it runs. Above the cards, counters show how many stations are solving and how many are in inspection.  Each card shows the station's name, the competitor at it and its state:  Waiting - no solve in progressInspection - inspection is running, with the inspection timeSolving - the timer is running, with the running timeFinished - the solve has ended, with its timeOffline - the station hasn't sent anything for 30 seconds  When the round has a cumulative time limit (for example in blindfolded events), the card shows Cumulative limit: the time the competitor has left, out of the whole limit. Last solve shows the station's last entered attempt. When a room runs more than one round, or a station is set to a round its room isn't running, the card also shows the station's round.

searchDocs.title: Live solving in the panel​
searchDocs.content: Who can use it: every signed-in user, when the competition uses FKMTime devices.  Click Live solving in the sidebar (or open /results/live). It's the same board, with a few additions for staff:  every station is listed, also ones that haven't sent anything yet, and the counters include how many stations are offlinefor delegates and users with delegate access, when a station calls the delegate, its card gets a red border and an Incident badge, and the page plays a sound

searchDocs.title: Public view of the results​
searchDocs.content: Who can use it: every signed-in user, when the competition uses FKMTime devices.  The panel has a copy of the public results, called Public view. It works the same way as Results on the public display.  Delegates open it from a round in Results: in the round's more actions menu (…), click Public view.Everyone else gets the public view when they click Results in the sidebar.  Signed-in users can also find Public display and TV view in the search at the top of the panel (on a computer; the phone layout has no search).

searchDocs.title: Server logs in the panel​
searchDocs.content: Admins can read the server logs in the panel: click Server logs on the Competition page, or go to /logs. Recent history shows first. Other roles can't open this page.  note The backend's own log is written only when BACKEND_LOGS_DIR is set for the backend, as in the FIM templates. Without it, the page says the backend log isn't available.

searchDocs.title: Docker logs​
searchDocs.content: You can also access logs with docker logs command. Just run this command in the directory with the docker-compose.yml file:  docker compose logs -f

searchDocs.title: Dumping the database​
searchDocs.content: Run the following command in the directory with the instance'sdocker-compose.yml file:  docker compose exec -T database pg_dump -d fkm_time > dump.sql   This command will dump the database to the dump.sql file on the host machine.  You can read about importing the database into development environment in the Importing database dump section.

searchDocs.title: Rounds​
searchDocs.content: Pick a round from the round list. The page opens on the round in progress, or the first round. The round's results are in a table with each attempt, the average and the best.    Search by name, WCA ID or ID filters the table.Ranking orders the results by place, Latest by the most recently changed.The line above the table shows the round's format, time limit, cutoff and who proceeds to the next round.  Each row has View attempts (opens the result, see A single result) and a menu with Delete result.

searchDocs.title: WCA Integrated Live Results​
searchDocs.content: When results go to WCA Integrated Live Results and FKMTime is connected to it, the round list shows the state of each round there (not open yet, open, done or needs attention), and each result shows how it is doing:  Sending - on its wayNot accepted, Not in round or Can't be sent - it isn't getting through; hover over the badge for the reasonDiffers - WCA live results holds other attempts than FKMTimeAdvances or May advance - the WCA's advancing flag  A row's menu also has Clear in WCA live results (empties the result there; FKMTime then sends its own again) and, in later rounds, Remove from round for a competitor who hasn't competed in it. Results that are only in WCA live results show up in the table too, with Clear in WCA live results.

searchDocs.title: Round actions​
searchDocs.content: Above the table:  Enter attempt - opens a form to enter an attempt for any competitor of the round: Competitor, Attempt, the time, Penalty, Outcome and, under More details, Judge, Scrambler, Station and Comment. A time over the time limit is saved as DNF.Enter scorecard - type in a competitor's paper scorecard, attempt by attempt.Double check - go through the round's results one competitor at a time. It shows once the round has results.  Enter scorecard and Double check are described in Double check and scorecards.  The round's menu (⋮) has:  Public view - the round as the public results show it.Resubmit to WCA Live (or to WCA Integrated Live Results, or Cubing Contests for unofficial events) - sends the whole round again, overwriting it there.When FKMTime is connected to WCA Integrated Live Results, actions for the round there, depending on its state: Open in WCA Integrated Live Results, Add competitor to round (first rounds), Close in WCA Integrated Live Results, View on WCA live results and Clear in WCA Integrated Live Results.Restart group - pick a group and confirm: all results from that group are deleted and its attendance is cleared. Use it when a group has to be run again.

searchDocs.title: Entering an attempt quickly​
searchDocs.content: Enter attempt at the top of every page (on phones, the floating button on the Results page) opens a keyboard-first form: pick one of the rounds in progress if the round isn't chosen already, type a competitor's name or registrant ID, the next attempt is picked for you, type the time, choose the Penalty (None, +2, +4, DNF or DNS) and press Enter to save. Enter attempt on a room's card on Home opens the same form for that room's round.

searchDocs.title: A single result​
searchDocs.content: View attempts opens a competitor's result in a round. You can also get there from an incident.    At the top:  Average and Best, and how many attempts are entered.Limits & warnings - the time limit (and how much of a cumulative limit is used and remaining), the cutoff, the number of attempts, and warnings such as Differs from WCA Live or Staffed before competing.Last attempt - the latest attempt with its stackmat time, inspection and judge, buttons to edit it, give an extra or delete it, and +2 and DNF to set its penalty in one click.WCA live results - only when FKMTime is connected to WCA Integrated Live Results: whether the result is Confirmed, Sending, Differs or Not sent yet, FKMTime's attempts next to the WCA's, and Clear in WCA live results.  The attempts are in tabs:  Submitted - the attempts that count, as sent to the results website, with judge, scrambler, station, comment, when each was solved, who edited it and its warningsStandard and Extra attempts (when there are extras) - every attempt, also showing what replaced it and its status. Standard has Swap attempts, to swap two attempts that were entered in the wrong orderReorder & extras - drag attempts into the right order, and drag an extra onto the attempt it replaces  Each attempt has:  Edit attempt - change the attempt number, time, penalty, outcome, judge, scrambler, station or comment. The result is resubmitted.Edit history - every change to the attempt: what changed, who changed it and when.Give extra attempt - the competitor gets an extra in place of this attempt. Add a comment or use a quick action.Delete attempt, after you confirm.

searchDocs.title: The result's menu​
searchDocs.content: The Enter attempt button next to the competitor's name adds an attempt to this result. The menu (⋮) next to it has:  Give extras for several attempts - when more than one attempt has to be redone, for example after a scramble mistake. Tick the Attempts to replace, choose Extra scrambles or a Fresh set (the normal scrambles of a set this competitor hasn't seen, like the next group's), add a comment and confirm. The page then shows the replaced attempts next to their extras, and you can switch which of them is Counting: the Originals or the Extras.DNF all attempts - a DNF ruling. Tick the attempts to set to DNF and add a comment. The times are kept. You can also DNF all the remaining attempts, so the competitor can't do any more. If the competitor has results in later rounds, Remove results in later rounds (Regulation 9t) removes them too. Afterwards the result shows the attempts Ruled DNF with Restore original attempts to undo the ruling.Resubmit scorecard to WCA Live (or the competition's results website) - sends this result again.Assign DNS on remaining attempts - when the competitor won't do the rest of their attempts.Remove from this round (Regulation 9t) - in later rounds, for a competitor who shouldn't have been in the round, for example after a score-taking mistake in the previous round. Give the Reason and confirm. The result then shows Removed from this round under Regulation 9t with Bring back to undo it.Delete result - deletes every attempt of the result.  DNF all attempts asks you to resolve the competitor's open incident first. Give extras for several attempts works with one open incident, which then gets its extra too, but not with more.

searchDocs.title: Checks​
searchDocs.content: Checks lists attempts worth a second look, for one round or All rounds. Filter them by type:  Inspection - inspection over 15 secondsPenalty - a penalty bigger than +2DNSFast - much faster than the competitor's other attempts in the roundStaffing - the competitor was recorded as judging or scrambling before a later solve in the same group    View attempts opens the result, where you can fix the attempt.

searchDocs.title: Importing scrambles​
searchDocs.content: Generate the scrambles in TNoodle and export them as encrypted scrambles JSON. Remember the password you chose: FKMTime never stores it, and the scrambling device asks for it before it shows any scrambles.  Go to Scrambles → Import and drop the file on Upload encrypted scrambles JSON (or click it to pick the file). FKMTime checks the file and lists every round and set it found, for example Set A · 5 scrambles · 2 extra.    What the check can show:  Errors detected during import - a set contains scrambles that aren't encrypted. You can't import the file until you export it again with encryptionWarnings detected during import - a round has no scrambles, has a different number of sets than the competition expects, or has sets with an unusual number of scrambles or extras (for example a Bo3 round instead of Ao5). Warnings don't stop the import; check that they are intentional    Events that aren't part of the competition are left out of the import. For an unofficial event, add it in Unofficial events first (see Unofficial events).  Click Import to save the scrambles, or Clear to pick another file. Only import rounds that don't have scrambles yet: if any set in the file was already imported, FKMTime refuses the whole file and tells you which set it was. To add more scrambles to a round later, use Add scramble set below.

searchDocs.title: Scramble sets​
searchDocs.content: The Scramble sets tab lists every round with the number of sets it has, or Missing if it has none yet. Click a round to see its sets and how many scrambles and extras each has.    Add scramble set - adds sets to the round, for example when you need a fresh set. In TNoodle, generate a file with only the new set, for this same event and round: FKMTime saves each set under the round named in the file. Upload it under Upload scrambles and click Add. The dialog says which letter the new sets start fromDelete scramble set (in the set's menu) - deletes one setDelete sets for this round (in the menu next to Add scramble set) - deletes every set of the selected roundDelete all scramble sets (same menu) - deletes the sets of every round, for example to start the import again    Deleting can't be undone; FKMTime asks you to confirm first.

searchDocs.title: Scrambling devices​
searchDocs.content: Every laptop or tablet used for scrambling is added as a scrambling device in a room. It offers Scramble only for rounds that are running in its room.  Go to Scrambles → Scrambling devices and click Add device. Enter a Name, choose the Room and click Save.    To sign the device in, click One-time login code (the key icon) next to it. FKMTime shows a 6-digit code. The code works for 10 minutes and only once. Opening the dialog again shows a new code and cancels the previous one. When a browser signs in with a new code, any browser signed in earlier as this scrambling device stops working and has to be signed in again.    The device's menu has Edit (change name or room) and Delete device.

searchDocs.title: On the scrambling device​
searchDocs.content: The scrambling device is a laptop or tablet with a web browser and a card reader that types the card number and presses Enter (like a keyboard). You can also type the card number by hand and press Enter.

searchDocs.title: Signing in​
searchDocs.content: Open FKMTime on the device and click Scrambling device on the sign-in page. The button is there only when Use FKMTime devices is on.    On the Scrambling device page, type the 6-digit code from One-time login code into the boxes. FKMTime sends it as soon as the sixth digit is typed (or click Continue). Wrong code means the code is mistyped, already used, replaced by a newer code, or older than 10 minutes. Back to staff sign in goes back to the usual sign-in.    The device stays signed in until you click Log out on its home page, until it is signed in again with a new code, or until the device is deleted.

searchDocs.title: Choosing a set​
searchDocs.content: The home page, Scramble sets, shows the device's room in the header. Pick the event at the top; events and rounds running in the room are marked with a dot. When an event has more than one round, pick the round next to its name. Until you pick something, the device shows the round running in its room.  Under the round name you can see whether it's running in the room: In progress in this room · Group 1, Running at a station (when a delegate used Run a different round… on a station of this room, see Managing devices), or Not in progress in this room.    For a round that is running in the room, each set has a Scramble button. Its menu (⋮) has All scrambles. For other rounds, sets only have All scrambles.

searchDocs.title: Scrambling​
searchDocs.content: Click Scramble next to the set you are using. Enter the password of the scrambles file and click Unlock. A wrong password shows Invalid password. Scan the scrambler's card. The scrambler signs every attempt scrambled on this device, so they scan in each time a set is opened. Scan the competitor's card. FKMTime picks the competitor's next attempt and shows its scramble: the competitor's name and WCA ID (or Newcomer), the scramble number (Scramble 1, or Extra 1 for an extra attempt a delegate granted with Extra scrambles; when the delegate chose Fresh set, the device shows the normal Scramble number, so open a set the competitor hasn't used), the scramble and a picture of the scrambled puzzle. Scramble the puzzle and click Sign. Cancel goes back without signing.  After signing, the device shows Last signed: with the competitor and scramble number, and waits for the next competitor's card.    Signing records the attempt as scrambled by this scrambler, at this time. On the competitor's result page the attempt shows as Scrambled, not solved yet, with the scrambler in the Scrambler column, until the station sends the solve. If the competitor's card is scanned again before they solve, the device shows the same scramble again.  Messages you may see when scanning:  Scrambler not found - no one has this card. Assign it on the Persons page (see Assigning cards)Competitor not foundScrambler and competitor cannot be the sameNo attempts left - the competitor has done all attempts of the round  If you open a set of a round that isn't running in the room, the device warns: This round isn't running in this room. Check that this is the right set before scrambling. The device doesn't notice a group change while a set is open, so go back to the home page when the room moves on.

searchDocs.title: Other options​
searchDocs.content: Change scrambler - when another person takes over scrambling; scan their card All scrambles - every scramble and extra of the set, after entering the password. Useful to check a scramble without signing anything Scan sounds (speaker icon in the header) - plays a sound on every successful or failed scan. It's off by default and saved on this device Log out - on the home page; the device needs a new one-time login code to sign in again

searchDocs.title: Requirements​
searchDocs.content: A Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge or Opera) on desktop.The page must be served over HTTPS (the public docs site is - Web Serial will not work over plain HTTP, except on localhost).A USB cable that supports data (not just power) and the device set to bootloader/download mode if required.  The latest firmware for each hardware revision is shown first. Use theShow older versions button to access previous releases.  Loading flasher…

searchDocs.title: Troubleshooting​
searchDocs.content: "Web Serial not supported" - switch to Chrome, Edge or Opera on a desktop OS.Device not detected - try another USB cable / port, and make sure no other program (serial monitor, IDE) is holding the port open.Flash fails partway through - perform a full chip erase by re-running the flasher; the installer offers an erase option on first install.  If problems persist, see the debugging section or open an issue on GitHub.

searchDocs.title: Running natively​
searchDocs.content: Clone the repo and run the manager directly with Python:  git clone https://github.com/FKMTime/fim cd fim python3 manager.py   Then open http://localhost:8181 in your browser.

searchDocs.title: Running in Docker​
searchDocs.content: The manager needs the host Docker socket so it can spin up FKMTime instances on the host.  export FIM_DATA_DIR=/opt/fim mkdir -p $FIM_DATA_DIR docker compose up -d   Override FIM_DATA_DIR in a .env file beside docker-compose.yml if you want a different path.  Same-path bind mount FKMTime instance templates use relative bind mounts (e.g. ./db,./logs). Docker Compose resolves these to absolute paths and passes them to the host Docker daemon, so the data directory must be mounted at the same absolute path inside and outside the container. That is what FIM_DATA_DIR does.  For a manual docker run:  docker run -d \ -p 8181:8181 \ -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ -v /opt/fim:/opt/fim \ -e FIM_DATA_DIR=/opt/fim \ fim

searchDocs.title: Creating an instance​
searchDocs.content: In the Instances card, click New instance.Pick a Template — prod for a real competition, dev for a demo instance that signs in against the dummy WCA services — enter a Nameand click Create.Open the Env tab and fill in the environment variables (seeSetup for production), then click Save.Back in the Control tab, click Start next to the instance.  The instance's logs are available in the panel, seeAccessing logs.

searchDocs.title: Wi-Fi on OpenWRT​
searchDocs.content: On OpenWRT, the WiFi tab sets the Hotspot that FKMTime devices connect to and the Uplink network that gives the router internet access. You can also set a Backup uplink, such as a phone hotspot: when the uplink has had no internet for a minute, FIM switches to the backup, and switches back once the uplink works again.

searchDocs.title: BLE and mDNS on Docker Desktop (macOS / Windows)​
searchDocs.content: On macOS and Windows, Docker Desktop runs containers inside a Linux VM, so containers do not have direct access to the host's Bluetooth or mDNS stack. That breaks BLE pairing of FKMTime stations and fkmtime.localdiscovery out of the box. (On Linux this just works because Docker is native.)  The fix is the same in both cases: rundocker-adapter on the host. It's a small standalone binary that forwards the host's BLE and mDNS into the FKMTime containers, so device pairing and *.localresolution work just like on Linux. The same adapter is used on both macOS and Windows; only the binary differs.  micro-connector probes the docker-adapter host port at startup and automatically uses it if it's available, so this works for anyFKMTime instance, regardless of whether it was started by FIM, bydocker compose up, or by hand.

searchDocs.title: With FIM (easiest)​
searchDocs.content: FIM's only job here is to download docker-adapter for you and keep it running, so you don't have to start it manually after every reboot.  caution The auto-adapter feature is only available when FIM is runningnatively. If FIM itself is running inside Docker, it cannot spawn or supervise host binaries, so the Adapter tab will not work. On macOS and Windows you should always run FIM natively; use the manual install below if you really need FIM in Docker for some reason.  Run FIM natively (not in Docker), as shownabove.Open the Adapter tab in FIM's web UI.Click the install/enable button. FIM grabs the right binary from thedocker-adapter releasesand runs it in the background.

searchDocs.title: Without FIM (manual)​
searchDocs.content: docker-adapter is a standalone binary, not a Docker container, so you don't need FIM at all to use it.  Download the matching build for your platform (macOS arm64 / x64, Windows x64) from thedocker-adapter releases page.Run the binary.Keep it running while your FKMTime instance is up. Start your instance the usual way (e.g. docker compose up); micro-connector will detect the adapter on its own.

searchDocs.title: Clone the production repository (and navigate into it)​
searchDocs.content: git clone https://github.com/FKMTime/production cd production

searchDocs.title: Environment variables​
searchDocs.content: Copy the .env.example file to .env and fill in the required fields.  cp .env.example .env   Variable	What it isTOKEN	Token for our proxy server SECRET	Random secret, at least 32 characters. It signs sign-in sessions and encrypts the WCA tokens stored in the database, so keep it the same for the whole competition WCA_CLIENT_ID, WCA_CLIENT_SECRET	WCA OAuth application credentials WCA_ORIGIN, WCA_LIVE_API_ORIGIN, CUBING_CONTESTS_API_ORIGIN	Addresses of the WCA website, WCA Live and Cubing Contests; keep the defaults BACKEND_ORIGIN, REDIRECT_SSL	Keep the defaults  For now, contact us and we will send you the proxy token and WCA OAuth credentials. Server will be running locally, but will be accessible from the internet through our proxy server.  Generate SECRET yourself, for example with:  openssl rand -hex 32   warning The backend refuses to start without a SECRET of at least 32 characters.  We are using fkm-proxy for proxying requests to the server. You can find more information about it in the repository.

searchDocs.title: Start the server​
searchDocs.content: Run the following command to start the server:  docker compose up   This will start backend, micro-connector, database and frontend.

searchDocs.title: Running tests​
searchDocs.content: The fake server replaces the normal backend, so stop the backend (and any other micro-connector) before running it.  The fake server reads tests.json from the current directory. This file defines groups, cards and optional rounds (attempt counts, cutoffs and time limits in centiseconds). The one in the repository has sample cards and groups.  To start it, go to the micro-connector project dir and run:  cargo run --bin e2e   Then run the micro-connector itself (cargo run) with the same SOCKET_PATH, so devices connect to the fake server.  Docker​  There is also a way to start the fake server and micro-connector together using docker. Just build the images:  docker compose build   And then run them:  docker compose up

searchDocs.title: Unit tests​
searchDocs.content: cd backend && npm run test:no-watch cd frontend && npm run test:no-watch

searchDocs.title: Backend E2E tests​
searchDocs.content: Backend E2E tests need PostgreSQL and the dummy WCA services. Start them with the test stack in the root directory of the project:  docker compose -f docker-compose-test.yml up -d   Go to the backend directory and create the database tables  cd backend npx prisma db push   Seed the database with test data  npm run prisma:seed-test   The test seed imports the competition that the dummy WCA generates, so its schedule starts on the day the dummy WCA started. To reset the database later, run npm run prisma:reset and seed it again.  Run the tests  npm run test:e2e

searchDocs.title: Browser E2E tests​
searchDocs.content: Browser tests start the backend and frontend themselves and use the same test stack. Run npm ci in backend and frontend first, then:  cd e2e npm ci npx playwright install chromium npx playwright test   To run a single file, pass it to Playwright, for examplenpx playwright test tests/auth.spec.ts.  note The tests run in GitHub Actions on pull requests that change the code they cover, so you can check their status there.
